conclusions: Default tracing and trace-off fixed series each retain one failure; tracing is not a necessary trigger in these samples.
No monitored native media property access exceeded 20 ms, while page heartbeat gaps around 5 seconds appeared in passed and failed samples.
Unassisted native metadata restoration reset the position near zero in all six WebKit controls.
All six directly corrected native controls restored their position; two show a roughly 5-second heartbeat gap without ArtPlayer loaded.
Deferred correction also leaves a 5.104-second heartbeat gap; no setTimeout workaround was adopted.
Same native direct-control entry passes Chromium/Firefox once each.
limitations: Property access instrumentation covers currentTime,duration,readyState,seeking,playbackRate,paused only; methods/layout/renderer/OS scheduling are not individually profiled.
Five-second gaps outside ArtPlayer do not prove the exact cause of every earlier ten-second timeout.
Each prospective series has a fixed repeat count and no failure retry; these are diagnostic samples, not statistical release certification.

Final helper adds a selector for the native page; correction and deferred control modes were added after their preceding preserved runs. No claim that final diagnostic source was identical across all controls.
Initial native failures retain their position assertion; not converted to expected passes or included in routine CI.
No production workaround, larger timeout, changed browser target, physical-device or remote CI acceptance.
